Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-ʿAnkabut (the Spider), because the spider is mentioned in it, unlike any other surah, and because it draws a parable for the polytheists: the feebleness of their taking idols as allies besides Allah is likened to the feebleness of a spider's web, which it takes as its house, and it is the weakest of houses.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Clarifying Allah's way (sunnah) regarding the trials of His friends (awliyaʾ), and that walking in this religion with sincerity is surrounded by affliction and tribulation. Through this, the believer whose heart is sincere in his loyalty to his religion and his steadfastness is distinguished from the hypocrite, whose tongue says what his heart opposes; and Allah, glorified and exalted, promises victory to the believing mujahidin and guidance to the straight path, and humiliation to the people of polytheism and their helpers.

• Establishing the proof for resurrection (baʿth) by considering the beginning of creation, which is more wondrous than its reproduction.

• Mention of the stories of some of the deniers among the nations and individuals, such as ʿAd, Thamud, Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman, and the destruction and ruin that befell them because of the polytheism, arrogance and tyranny in which they engaged.

• Mention of the evidences for the existence of Allah, may He be exalted, and His oneness in this universe, and binding the polytheists to affirm His oneness by their acknowledgment that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and the Manager of this universe. Within this is a reminder of the blessings with which Allah has favored them, so that they may desist from worshipping anything other than Him.

• The command to the Prophet ﷺ to remain steadfast in conveying the Qur'an and establishing the laws of Islam, and clarifying the truthfulness of his message, and establishing the truth of the Qur'an by the unlettered (ummiyyah) state of the one to whom it was revealed ﷺ, and that is the greatest proof of the soundness of his prophethood.

• Warning the polytheists of the punishment they sought to hasten in mockery, and that it will come at its appointed time suddenly, and affirming the recompense for their deeds, and encouraging the believers with the reward they will have upon returning to Allah, for their patience in obeying Him and their bearing of harm in His way.

[Tafsir]

﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqattaʿah) has already preceded at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah.
Do the people think that when they say, "We have believed," Allah will leave them without trial or testing?

And We had certainly tested those who came before them among the nations, and tried them, those to whom We sent Our messengers, so that Allah would make manifest to the creation the truthfulness of the truthful in their faith and the falsehood of the liars, so that each group would be distinguished from the other.

Rather, do those who commit evil deeds, including polytheism and other sins, think that they can outpace Us, escaping Us by themselves so that We cannot take hold of them? Evil is their judgment, the judgment they pass.

Whoever hopes to meet God and longs for His reward, then surely the term God has appointed for raising His creatures to be recompensed with reward and punishment is coming soon. And He is the All-Hearing of words, the All-Knowing of deeds.

And whoever strives in the cause of raising high the word of Allah, and strives against his own self by compelling it to obedience, then he strives only for his own benefit, because he does that seeking the reward for his striving. Indeed, Allah is free of need from the deeds of all His creatures; to Him belong the dominion, the creation, and the command.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 29 (al-ʿAnkabūt), verse 7:

﴿And those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their misdeeds, and We will surely reward them for their good deeds with the best of what they used to do.﴾

And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents, that he should be good to them in word and deed. But if they strive with you, O man, to make you associate with Me in worship, then do not obey them. To the same category as the call to associate partners with Allah belongs every other act of disobedience: there is no obedience to any created being, whoever he may be, in disobedience to Allah the Glorified, as has been established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). To Me is your return on the Day of Resurrection, and I will inform you of what you used to do in the world, of righteous and wicked deeds, and I will recompense you for them.
And those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did righteous deeds, We will surely admit them into Paradise among the company of Allah's righteous servants.

And among the people is one who says, "We believe in God," but when he is harmed for it by the polytheists, he recoils from their punishment and harm just as he would recoil from the punishment of God, and he does not endure the injury they inflict. So he renounces his faith. And if victory comes from your Lord, O Messenger, to the people of faith in Him, these apostates from their faith will surely say, "We were with you, O believers, supporting you against your enemies." Is not God more knowing than every person of what is in the breasts of all His creatures?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verse 11:

Allah will surely make manifest His knowledge to the creatures, those who affirmed that Allah and His Messenger are true and acted according to His law. And He will surely make manifest His knowledge of the hypocrites, so that each group may be distinguished from the other.

And those who disbelieved in the Oneness of God from among the Quraysh, and did not believe in His threat and His promise, said to those among them who affirmed God and acted according to His law: "Abandon the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ) and follow our religion, for we will bear the burdens of your sins." But they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars in what they claimed.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verse 13:

﴿And those disbelievers shall surely bear their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they shall surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.﴾

We sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them for a thousand years less fifty years, calling them to monotheism (al-Tawhid) and forbidding them from associating partners with God (shirk). They did not respond to him, so God destroyed them by the flood, and they were wrongdoers toward themselves through their disbelief and transgression.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verse 15:

So We saved Noah and those who followed him and were with him in the ship, and We made that an example and a lesson for all the worlds.

Mention, O Messenger, Abraham (peace be upon him) when he called his people: "Devote your worship to Allah alone, and guard yourselves against His wrath by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. That is better for you, if you only knew what is better for you and what is worse."

This is the commentary of al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex) on surah 29, verse 17.

"You worship, O people, besides Allah, only idols, and you fabricate a lie by calling them gods. Indeed, the idols you worship besides Allah cannot provide you with any sustenance. So seek your provision from Allah, not from your idols, and devote your worship and gratitude to Him for His provision to you. To Allah you will be returned after your death, and He will repay you for what you have done."

If you deny—O people—our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) in what he has called you to, namely worshipping Allah alone, then communities before you also denied their messengers in what they called them to of the truth, and the wrath of Allah befell them. The duty of the Messenger Muhammad is only to convey to you the message of Allah clearly, and he has done so.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verse 19:

Have these people not known how Allah originates creation from nothing, and then restores it after its perishing, just as He began it the first time, a new creation, nothing being beyond His capacity? Indeed, that is easy for Allah, just as its origination was easy for Him.

Say, [O Messenger], to those who deny resurrection after death: "Travel through the earth and observe how Allah originated creation. Was He incapable of initiating it? Likewise, He is not incapable of recreating it in the final creation. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent; nothing He wills is beyond His power."

He punishes whomever He wills of His creatures for the sins they committed during their lifetime, and He shows mercy to whomever He wills among them, those who repent, believe and do righteous deeds. To Him you will be returned, and He will repay you for what you have done.

You and mankind cannot escape Allah on the earth or in the heavens if you disobey Him. Besides Allah you have no protector to manage your affairs, nor any helper to defend you against Allah if He intends you harm.

Those who disbelieved in the proofs of God and denied His signs, and in the meeting with Him on the Day of Resurrection, those have no hope of My mercy in the Hereafter when they witness what has been prepared for them of punishment. And those will have a painful, agonizing punishment.

So the only answer of Abraham's people was that some of them said to others: "Kill him or burn him with fire." So they threw him into it, but God saved him from it and made it cool and safe for him. Indeed, in Our saving Abraham from the fire there are clear signs and proofs for a people who believe in God and act according to His law.

Ibrahim said to his people: "O my people, you have only taken idols besides Allah, and worship of them has bound you together in love and friendship during the life of this world. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disown others and curse one another. Your final abode is all the Fire, and you will have no helpers to save you from entering it."

Lot believed in Abraham and followed his creed. Abraham said: "I am leaving my people's homeland for the blessed land," which is "al-Sham" (Greater Syria). Indeed, He is the Mighty (al-'Aziz), whom none can overcome, the Wise (al-Hakim) in His management.

We granted him Isaac as a son, and Jacob after him as a grandson. We placed prophethood and the scriptures among his descendants, and We gave him his reward for his trials on Our behalf: in this world, a good name and righteous offspring, and in the Hereafter he is certainly among the righteous.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verses 28–29:

Mention, O Messenger, Lot, when he said to his people: "Indeed you commit an abominable deed (al-fahisha) that no one among the worlds has preceded you in. Do you indeed approach men in their rear passages, and cut off the roads of travelers by your wicked deed, and commit in your gatherings evil acts such as mocking people and pelting passersby with stones, and harming them with what is unseemly of speech and action?" In this is an announcement that it is not permissible for people to unite upon what is reprehensible of what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden. So the answer of Lot's people to him was only that they said: "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are among the truthful in what you say, and in fulfilling what you promise."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verses 28–29:

Mention, O Messenger, Lot, when he said to his people: "Indeed you commit an abominable deed (al-fahisha) that no one among the worlds has preceded you in. Do you indeed approach men in their rear passages, and cut off the roads of travelers by your wicked deed, and commit in your gatherings evil acts such as mocking people and pelting passersby with stones, and harming them with what is unseemly of speech and action?" In this is an announcement that it is not permissible for people to unite upon what is reprehensible of what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden. So the answer of Lot's people to him was only that they said: "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are among the truthful in what you say, and in fulfilling what you promise."
He said: "My Lord, help me against the corrupt people by sending down punishment upon them, since they invented this abomination and persisted in it." So God answered his supplication.

When the angels came to Ibrahim with the glad tidings from Allah of Ishaq, and of Ya'qub, Ishaq's son who would come after him, the angels said to Ibrahim: "Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of the town of the people of Lut, which is Sodom (Sadum). Its people were wrongdoers against themselves by their disobedience to Allah."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verse 32:

Abraham said to the angels: "Indeed, Lot is in it." They said: "We know best who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife, who will be among those who remain behind and are destroyed."

When Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed on their account and felt helpless to protect them, for he thought them to be human guests, and he grieved at their presence because he knew the wickedness of his people's deeds. They said to him: "Do not fear, nor grieve. Your people will not reach us. Do not grieve over what we have told you, that We will destroy them. We will surely save you and your family from the punishment that will descend upon your people, except your wife, for she is among those who will perish along with her people."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 29, verse 34:

We are going to send down upon the people of this town a punishment from the sky, because of their disobedience to Allah and their committing of indecency (al-fahisha).
"And We have left from the dwellings of the people of Lot clear signs for a people who reason, so that they may take heed and benefit from them."

We also sent to Midian their brother Shu'ayb, and he said to them: "O my people, worship Allah alone, and devote your worship sincerely to Him. You have no deity other than Him. Hope through your worship for the reward of the Last Day, and do not spread corruption and sins upon the earth, nor persist in them; rather, repent to Allah from them and turn back to Him in obedience."
The people of Madyan denied Shu'ayb in what he brought them from Allah of the message, so the severe earthquake seized them, and in the morning they were lying prostrate in their homes, dead.

And We destroyed ʿĀd and Thamūd. It has become clear to you from their dwellings that they were ruined and emptied of their inhabitants, and that Our punishment befell them all. Satan made their wicked deeds appear attractive to them and barred them from the way of Allah, from the path of faith in Him and in His messengers. They were perceptive in their disbelief and misguidance, admiring it, thinking that they were upon guidance and rightness, while in fact they were deeply immersed in error.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verse 39:

"And We destroyed Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman. Moses had certainly come to them with clear proofs, but they behaved arrogantly in the land, and they could not outrun Us; rather, We were able to overpower them."

So We seized each of those mentioned with Our punishment for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a fierce wind that pelted them with stones of baked clay, one after another; they were the people of Lut. Among them were those seized by the Blast (al-Sayhah), and they were the people of Salih and the people of Shu'ayb. Among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, like Qarun. And among them were those whom We drowned; they were the people of Nuh, Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his people. Allah would never destroy these people for the sins of others, wronging them by destroying them without deserving it. Rather, they wronged themselves by indulging in the blessings of their Lord and worshipping other than Him.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verse 41:

The likeness of those who take protectors other than Allah, hoping for their help, is like the spider that makes a house for itself to shelter it; but it does not avail it anything when it needs it. Likewise, these polytheists: their protectors whom they took besides Allah will not avail them anything. Indeed, the weakest of houses is the house of the spider. If they only knew this, they would not have taken them as protectors; for they neither benefit them nor harm them.

God knows what they associate with Him of rivals (andad), and that these are in reality nothing; they are merely names that they have invented, which neither benefit nor harm. And He is the Mighty (al-'Aziz) in His retribution against those who disbelieve in Him, the Wise (al-Hakim) in His management and His creation.
These parables We set forth for people, so that they may benefit from them and learn from them, and none grasp them except those who know God, His signs, and His law.

God created the heavens and the earth with truth and justice. Indeed, in His creating that there is a great sign of His power and of His being the sole deity, and He specified the believers in the mention, because they are the ones who benefit from it.

Recite what has been revealed to you of this Qur'an and act upon it, and establish the prayer (ṣalāh) with its prescribed limits. Indeed, maintaining the prayer restrains its performer from falling into acts of disobedience and evil deeds. That is because the one who observes it, completing its pillars and conditions, has his heart illuminated, his faith increased, and his desire for good strengthened, while his desire for evil diminishes or disappears. And the remembrance of Allah in the prayer and beyond it is greater, mightier, and more excellent than everything else. Allah knows what you do, good and evil, and He will reward you for it with the most complete and perfect reward.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verse 46:

Do not argue, O believers, with the Jews and the Christians except in the best manner, with gentle speech and beautiful words, and by calling to the truth by the easiest path that leads to it. Except for those who have deviated from the path of truth, obstinately persisted, shown arrogance, and declared war against you. Fight them until they believe, or until they give the jizya (a tax paid by non-Muslim subjects under Muslim rule) with their own hands while they are humbled. And say: "We believe in the Qur'an that has been revealed to us, and we believe in the Torah and the Gospel that were revealed to you. Our God and your God is one; He has no partner in His divinity, nor in His lordship, nor in His names and attributes. And we are submissive to Him, humbly obedient in what He has commanded us and what He has forbidden us."

And just as We sent down the Scriptures to those messengers before you, O Messenger, We have sent down to you this Book, which confirms the earlier Scriptures. Those to whom We gave the Book from the Children of Israel, who know it as it truly should be known, believe in the Qur'an. Among these Arabs, from the Quraysh and others, there are those who believe in it. None deny the Qur'an or doubt its clear proofs and evidences except the disbelievers, whose habit is denial and obstinacy.

Among your clear miracles, O Messenger, is that you did not read any book nor write any letters with your right hand before the Qur'an was revealed to you, and they know this. Had you been a reader or a writer before it was revealed to you, the falsifiers (al-mubtilun) would have doubted this, and they would have said: "He learned it from earlier books, or he copied it from them."

The Qur'an is rather clear signs, plain in their indication of the truth, preserved in the hearts of the scholars. None denies Our signs and rejects them except the wrongdoers who are stubborn, those who know the truth yet turn away from it.

The Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verse 50:

The polytheists said: "Why were not signs and proofs sent down upon Muhammad from his Lord, which we could witness, like the she-camel of Salih and the staff of Musa?" Say to them: "The matter of these signs belongs to Allah. If He wills, He sends them down; and if He wills, He withholds them. I am only a warner to you, warning you of the severity of His might and His punishment, and making clear the path of truth from falsehood."

Or is it not sufficient for these polytheists, in their knowledge of your truthfulness, O Messenger, that We have sent down to you the Qur'an, which is recited to them? Indeed, in this Qur'an is mercy for the believers, in this world and in the Hereafter, and a reminder through which they take heed, by the lesson and admonition it contains.

Say: "Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you, to attest to my truthfulness that I am His Messenger, and to your denial of me and your rejection of the truth I have brought from Allah. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth; nothing in them is hidden from Him. As for those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah, despite these clear proofs, it is they who are the losers in this world and the Hereafter."

The Noble Qur'an and its commentary: King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar), surah 29, verse 53:

They are asking you, O Messenger, to hasten the punishment, these disbelievers among your people, mocking. Had it not been that Allah had set for their punishment in this world an appointed time that neither advances nor delays, the punishment would have come upon them the moment they asked for it. It will certainly come upon them suddenly, while they are unaware of it and do not perceive it.

They urge you to hasten the punishment in this world, and it will surely come upon them, either in this world or in the Hereafter. Indeed, the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter will surround them on every side, and they will have no escape from it.

On the Day of Resurrection, the punishment of Hell will envelop the disbelievers from above their heads and from beneath their feet, so the Fire will surround them from all their directions. And God will say to them at that time: "Taste the recompense of what you used to do in the world: of associating partners with God, and committing crimes and sins."
O My servants who have believed, if you are in hardship in displaying your faith and worshipping Allah alone, then migrate to the wide earth of Allah, and devote your worship to Me alone.
Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned for reckoning and recompense.

Those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did the righteous deeds they were commanded to do: We will surely lodge them in Paradise in lofty chambers beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. How excellent is the reward of those who act in obedience to Allah. These chambers are in the Gardens of Bliss.

Indeed, those gardens mentioned are for the believers who were patient in worshipping Allah, who held firmly to their religion, and who put their trust in Allah for their provision and in their struggle against their enemies.

And how many a creature does not store up its provision for the morrow, as the son of Adam does; yet Allah, glorified and exalted, provides for it just as He provides for you. And He is the All-Hearing of your speech, the All-Knowing of your deeds and the passing thoughts of your hearts.

This is the commentary on Qur'an 29:64 from the Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex).

"This worldly life is nothing but amusement and play. Hearts are diverted by it, and bodies are engaged in it, because of the adornment and desires it contains. Then it passes away swiftly. Indeed, the Hereafter is the true, lasting life, in which there is no death. If people knew this, they would not have preferred the abode of perishing over the abode of everlasting existence."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 29, verses 65–66:

When the disbelievers board ships at sea and fear drowning, they single out Allah and sincerely direct their supplication to Him alone in their hardship. But when He delivers them safely to land and the hardship passes from them, they return to their polytheism. Indeed, by this they are self-contradictory: they affirm Allah's oneness in the hour of hardship, and associate others with Him in the hour of ease. Their associating partners with Him after Our blessing upon them of deliverance from the sea is so that they may become ungrateful for what We have bestowed upon them, in themselves and their wealth, and so that they may complete their enjoyment of this worldly life. But they will soon come to know the corruption of their deed, and what Allah has prepared for them of painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection. In this is a threat and a warning to them.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 29, verse 68:

No one is more unjust than the one who lies against Allah, attributing to Allah the misguidance and falsehood he is upon, or who denies the truth with which Allah sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). Indeed, in the Fire is a dwelling for those who disbelieve in Allah, deny His Oneness, and reject His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

The believers who strive against the enemies of God, against the self, and against Satan, and who endure trials and harm for the sake of God, God will guide them to the paths of goodness and keep them firm upon the straight path. Whoever has this description is a doer of good to himself and to others. Indeed, God, glorified and exalted, is with those among His creation who do good, with support, assistance, protection and guidance.
